lines: There are two ways to grow a business. You can chase sales, one at a time, forever. Or you can build people, and let the people build the business. This is the path of a leader.
Here's a truth about human beings: everyone wants to be part of something bigger than themselves. Your job as a leader is to give them that.
Apex isn't just a set of tools. It's a mission — to help everyday people build real income by helping businesses grow. You're not offering a product. You're offering a purpose.
But a vision doesn't move on its own. It moves through leaders. You can't carry it alone — and you're not supposed to. You build a team of like-minded people to carry it with you.
So the real question isn't how many can I sell. It's who can I build. A business built on people you developed will outlast anything you could sell by yourself.
You're looking for like-minded people — who want to build, who want to help others, who want more for their life. Pour into them, and you don't just grow a team. You change lives.
Vision needs a system. And the Apex system is beautifully simple. It's built on two numbers: five, and three.
Five leaders. Three customers each. That's the whole engine. Everything you build, you build around those two numbers.
Step one — become a product of the product. Before you ever sell the tool, you use it. People don't buy the product. They buy your conviction.
Step two — get three customers. Not thirty. Three. Small enough that anyone can do it, and it's the proof the model works.
Step three — find five leaders. Five people who will do what you just did: use the tool, get their three customers, and lead their own team.
Step four — duplicate. You teach your five to find their five. Same simple steps, repeated down through your team.
Why does three matter so much? Because it's duplicatable. Big numbers scare people, and they quit. Three feels possible — so people actually do it, and teach it.
Five and three isn't a limit — it's a launch pad. Master it, teach it, and it repeats itself through your whole organization.
Now the most important skill of all — the one nobody teaches. How do you find those five leaders, and how do you develop them? This is where real leadership lives.
First, identify. You're not looking for the loudest person in the room. You're looking for the hungry, the coachable, the ones who genuinely want to help others.
And a leader is not someone you drag along. You don't chase, convince, or beg. You look for people already reaching for more, and you offer them a path.
Once you spot someone with potential, you develop them through conversation — not a pitch. There are three questions that change everything.
Question one: what do you want? Not from the business — for your life. More time? To be home with your kids? Get them talking about the dream behind the money.
Question two: how do you want to help? This uncovers the leader inside them. The ones who light up talking about helping others — those are your future leaders.
Question three: how much do you want to make? Get a real number. Their number tells you what to build toward, and how hard to work, together.
Then do the hardest thing in leadership: listen. Really listen. Their answers are the map. Connect what they want to what this can do.
Developing a leader isn't one talk. It's showing up. You do the first few with them, not for them. You believe in them out loud — before they believe in themselves.
When you pour into people this way, they don't just build a business. They become someone new. And loyalty like that, money can't buy.
So what does this build? Four ways to earn at once. Direct commissions on what you sell. Overrides on what your team sells. Rank bonuses as you grow. And a share of company bonus pools.
Picture it. You develop five leaders. They each develop five. That's thirty people — and you personally recruited only five.
With a team that size, all modestly active, a Silver leader can earn around seven hundred dollars a month — most of it from a team you led, not sold.
And that's the modest picture. Because the system duplicates, it doesn't add — it multiplies. Your income grows even when you're not the one selling.
So here's the whole path. Cast a vision people want to belong to. Live the product. Get your three. Find your five. And develop them with real conversations.
Build people, and the business builds itself. That's leadership. That's Apex. Now — go find your five.
